clue.text: Ford Capri starts making constant power – it’s hot

indicators.note: the opening letter of the car model is made into something else, so one letter is swapped for another at its start

blocks.note: the Ford Capri, a car model, taken as written
c is the symbol for a constant (the speed of light)
P is the abbreviation for power
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: A boast that a classic Ford Capri suddenly develops serious engine power and is a hot car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford Capri' reads as one car, but Ford supplies the Ka and Capri has its C swapped for P to make PAPRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a red pepper spice, and the hotter varieties give real fiery heat to food.

clue.text: A classic Doctor Who fan may finally start to manufacture Tardis for one

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the preceding words in turn
the start of the following word means just its opening letter is used

blocks.clueFragment: A classic Doctor Who fan may
blocks.note: the last letter of each of these six words
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A devoted fan of vintage Doctor Who might end up building a replica of the Tardis.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a fan building a prop; really it collects word endings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardis stands for Time And Relative Dimension In Space, so it is an example of a word formed from initial letters.

clue.text: They have faith in Gunners – with group of footballers blocking big shot and Isak’s header

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one piece is lodged within another
a header is the top of something, so only the opening letter of the name is taken

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
a big shot is a celebrity or star
the Football Association, English football's governing body
the first letter of the striker's name

explanation.surface: A football report: Arsenal (the Gunners) score as a crowd of players block a shot and Isak heads in.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunners suggests Arsenal, the football club, but in crosswords it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafari are followers of the Rastafarian religious movement originating in Jamaica, a body of believers.

clue.text: Sticky chicken ultimately overdone in Kentucky

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the bird is used
in places the preceding pieces within the abbreviation of the state

blocks.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
the last letter of the word
OTT means over the top

explanation.surface: Fried chicken in Kentucky cooked too long ends up gooey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fast-food meal; overdone means over the top, not overcooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is a tricky, awkward one, just as a knotty problem is hard to untangle.

clue.text: Guide a Dutch cap’s sticky-out bit

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Dutch
the peak projecting from the front of a cap

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek guidebook entry on the jutting part of a Dutch cap.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dutch cap is also a contraceptive device, which makes the surface cheeky; here the cap is simply headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide is a person who counsels or steers others, and an advisor does exactly that job.

clue.text: After demolition derbies, carbon is present

indicators.note: demolition knocks things down so the material can be rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: After a demolition derby, carbon soot hangs in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolition derbies' reads as a car-smashing event; 'present' looks like a word about being there but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a case or picture is to set it out in words, giving an account, which is to describe it.

clue.text: Plans from 15th of March, say to host 1st of April

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so the date surrounds the following piece
the first of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the Ides of March falls on the 15th; 'say' marks it as one example of ides
the first letter of the month

explanation.surface: Diary planning: something arranged for mid-March and the start of April.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Roman calendar the ides fell on the 15th of March, May, July and October.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans are schemes or proposals in mind, and ideas covers the same sense of notions about what to do.

clue.text: By all conclusions two or three turn over a new leaf?

indicators.note: taking every conclusion means using the final letter of each word in turn
one thing placed over another covers it, so the verb wraps around the following letters

blocks.note: the last letters of these three words
a turn in a game is a go
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone resolves, after a couple of tries, to turn over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over a new leaf' reads as an idiom for reform, but the leaf alone is the definition and 'over' wraps GO round A N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb whose aromatic dried leaves are used in cooking, so it is one kind of leaf; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Discovered both deer and giraffe somehow accept not seeing eye to eye

definitions.text: accept not seeing eye to eye

indicators.note: with its cover taken off, a word loses its outside letters and only the middle stays
somehow says the letters end up arranged in some unspecified way

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wildlife find: a deer and a giraffe that somehow don't see eye to eye, given their heights.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a giraffe and a deer could never literally see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to differ is to accept a disagreement amicably and stop arguing, which is acknowledging the two sides will not concur.

clue.text: Quickly stop cycling around on …

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, the front ones going to the back
around means the cycled letters sit on either side of the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
re means on, as in 'on the subject of'

explanation.surface: A cyclist is told to stop pedalling around and get on, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis just runs the surface into the next clue; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical tempo marking meaning at a fast pace, and is also used as an exclamation for something done rapidly.

clue.text: … high gears – satisfied punctures must be what accounts for energy consumption

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are out of their senses and jumbled
something that punctures goes into another, so it sits inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a need that is satisfied has been met

explanation.surface: A cyclist in high gears gets a puncture, read on from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like it describes the gears, but it signals a shuffle, as in being high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter is the device recording how much gas a household uses, so it accounts for its fuel usage.

clue.text: Sailor’s objective? Get lost

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so the named letters drop out

blocks.note: an objective is a target
the letters removed, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor's aim is questioned, followed by a rude brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get lost' reads as an insult, but it says to remove GET from TARGET. Tar is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is a traditional nickname for a seaman, so tar is a crossword staple word for a mariner.

clue.text: Maybe comic books I reordered will be undamaged

indicators.note: reordered says the parts listed are set down in a different sequence

blocks.note: a comic's routine is an example of an act
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: Comic books rearranged on the shelf will come to no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic books' looks like a single item, but it splits into an act and NT; the three pieces are then placed in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and unharmed, not broken or impaired, the same state as being undamaged.

clue.text: Old Italian curate’s travelling north

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move, so the letters shift out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian clergyman is heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were a people of ancient Italy, living in Etruria before Rome rose to power.

clue.text: Coat brand Mark is wearing

indicators.note: a garment that is worn wraps around the wearer, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to brand is to sear with a hot iron
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark has on a coat of a particular label.
explanation.walkthrough: Coat, brand and Mark all look like fashion words; brand is the verb for burning a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To coat a surface is to spread a layer over it, and to smear is to spread something greasy or sticky across it.

clue.text: Does he tend to hack Yahoo after turning on firm?

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: firm and steady
a yahoo is a loutish person, a yob

explanation.surface: A question whether someone hacks into Yahoo after turning on a company.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about computer hacking; a hack is also a riding horse. A yob is British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable boy is a lad who looks after horses, and a hack is a horse hired out for ordinary riding.

clue.text: Private is last to solve 10 and possibly 11 across assuming 5 is reversed

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter only
reversed means the short phrase before it is read backwards
to assume is to take on, so one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
X is ten in Roman numerals
the puzzle's own 11 across is an example of a clue
V is five in Roman numerals, followed by 'is' as written

explanation.surface: A tricky instruction that solving 10 and 11 across depends on reading 5 across backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like references to other entries, but 10 and 5 are Roman numerals; only 11 across really points at the grid, as an example of a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something private is restricted to particular people, just as an exclusive club or event keeps outsiders out.

clue.text: Jack and chairman stood on the counter to get bottle

indicators.note: counter suggests going against the direction, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
Chairman Mao, leader of Communist China
stood as in tolerated, endured, bore

explanation.surface: A pub scene: Jack and the chairman climb onto the bar to get a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' suggests a bar, but 'on the counter' means running contrary, so MAO BORE is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large wine or champagne bottle holding several standard bottles' worth.

clue.text: Problem with locks and rent stops

blocks.note: rent as the past tense of rend, torn apart
stops as a verb, finishes

explanation.surface: A landlord's troubles with door locks and rent arrears ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests doors and 'rent' money; here locks are hair and rent means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are hair strands frayed at the tips, a common complaint about tresses or locks of hair.

clue.text: Fed up – framed by force making assumption

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top
a picture framed by something has it all round its edges

blocks.note: Fed is the setter of this puzzle, so the setter's name stands for me
to force open is to prise

explanation.surface: Someone fed up after being set up, accused under duress.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed is this puzzle's setter, so the name gives ME; 'fed up' reads as weary.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a proposition taken as true and used as the basis of an argument, a starting assumption.

clue.text: Bitter’s free on account

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
to free of something is to rid of it

explanation.surface: A pub note: bitter beer is free, put on the tab.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale, which makes the surface a bar offer; here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, pungent taste or smell, harsh and unpleasant like something bitter.

clue.text: Record if the amp is occasionally set virtually

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept
virtually means almost, so the word is used without its final letter

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recording engineer checks whether the amplifier is set up right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'amp' suggest a music studio, but the record here is a verb meaning list.
explanation.definitionFit: To record things in detail is to list them one by one, which is what itemising a bill or inventory means.

clue.text: Airport in France is most lenient

blocks.note: LAX is the code for Los Angeles International Airport
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain French airport has the least strict security.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or not strict, so the superlative laxest describes whoever is least severe.

clue.text: Perhaps Violet Beauregarde’s second to go back after Wonka’s introduction – monstrous creature!

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the name is used
second points to the letter in position two of the surname
going back means the combined letters are read from end to start

blocks.note: the first letter of the name
a violet is an example of a flower
the second letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Violet Beauregarde, the gum-chewing girl in Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, swells into a monstrous blueberry after Wonka's warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet looks like the character's first name but works as an example of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a person of folklore who turns into a wolf at full moon, a fearsome mythical beast.

clue.text: 9’s keen

blocks.note: the answer to 9 down, read as an instruction: its first word with 'to differ' telling it to change

explanation.walkthrough: 9 down is AGREE TO DIFFER, which read cryptically says AGREE is to be made different, that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen is enthusiastic and impatient to act, the same as being eager to do something.

clue.text: Charm of drug smuggler passing through airport on vacation

indicators.note: someone passing through a place is inside it, so this piece goes within the other
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a mule is someone who carries drugs across borders

explanation.surface: A drug runner's lucky charm goes through airport security as they go on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' looks like going on holiday but means emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a trinket worn to ward off evil or bring luck, and a charm is such a protective object.

clue.text: Drive in motorsport – getting cross

blocks.note: F1, Formula One, with the 1 read as I
a cross is the shape X

explanation.surface: A Formula One driver loses their temper during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests racing, but 'Drive in' is the definition, as in driving in a nail; the digit 1 doubles as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive in a nail or stake is to secure it firmly in place, which is one sense of fix.

clue.text: Identify problem in San Diego unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong in San Diego and needs pinning down.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to determine the nature of an illness or fault, which is working out what the trouble is.

clue.text: Bring out psychedelic Italian trousers

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets or takes in, so the phrase holds the answer within it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A fashion item: a pair of trippy, brightly patterned Italian trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' reads as a noun, the clothing, but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it from someone, which is exactly to bring it out.

clue.text: Good lord – Mary’s swimming in river

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters shift into a new order
in places the jumbled name inside the river

blocks.note: the name, with 's read as 'is'
the Dee, a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: An alarmed exclamation on seeing Mary taking a swim in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay, interchangeable as old-fashioned expressions of shock.

clue.text: Small tent’s not finished before daughter gets soaked

indicators.note: something not finished is missing its end, so the final letter of the word goes

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a teepee is a conical tent
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A camping mishap: the tent wasn't fully pitched before a daughter got drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the shortened tent ahead of D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steeped has been left in liquid to soak through, like tea leaves or fruit, so it is soaked.
